title: How to customize the toolbar in Safari on Mac: add, move, and remove buttons
metaTitle: How to Customize the Toolbar in Safari on Mac | Lazur
description: How to customize the toolbar in Safari on Mac: add, move, and remove buttons with View > Customize Toolbar, plus fixes for a hidden or cut-off bar.
targetKeyword: how to customize the toolbar in safari on mac
intro: To customize the toolbar in Safari on Mac, choose View > Customize Toolbar, drag buttons onto or off the bar, and click Done. Hold Command and drag an item off the bar to remove it, or drag it along the bar to move it.
tldr: Choose View > Customize Toolbar, then drag buttons from the palette onto the bar.
Hold Command and drag a button off the bar to remove it.
Drag buttons along the bar to move them, or hold Command and drag them directly on the toolbar.
Click Done to finish. If the bar is hidden, choose View > Show Toolbar first.
Apple's steps are documented for macOS 27 and Safari 27.0.

blocks.text: The Safari toolbar holds the buttons you use most, from Back and Forward to the address field. You can add buttons, remove them, and change their order with Apple's built-in tools, so you don't need extra software. This guide follows Apple's current help pages, which show macOS 27 and Safari 27.0. Older releases may label a few things differently.
Open the Customize Toolbar screen in Safari

Start with Safari open and a window in front of you. Click View in the menu bar, then choose Customize Toolbar. The toolbar switches into edit mode, and a palette of buttons appears. Every change in this guide starts from that screen.

If the toolbar is hidden, you can't customize it yet. Choose View > Show Toolbar first. Apple's Mac Help lists both Hide Toolbar and Show Toolbar under View, so the item you see depends on the current state.
Add a button to the Safari toolbar

In edit mode, find the button you want in the palette. Drag it toward the bar. Keep dragging until a plus sign appears under the pointer. Apple's Mac Help describes this exact step, so wait for the plus sign before you let go.
You can move the button again later, so the first spot doesn't have to be perfect. Make one change, look at the bar, then make the next one. That habit saves you from undoing a whole row of work.
Remove a button from the Safari toolbar

Removing is the step most people find surprising. Hold the Command (⌘) key, then drag the button off the bar. Let go when it leaves the bar, and it disappears. Apple's guide says to click Done when you finish.

A plain drag doesn't remove anything. Plain drags add buttons and reorder them. Only Command-drag takes a button off the bar. You can bring a removed button back from the palette whenever you want it.
Move buttons around the toolbar

You can reorder buttons in two ways. In edit mode, drag a button left or right along the bar. Or hold Command and drag the button on the toolbar, which Apple says rearranges it directly. Both methods work for most buttons.

Apple lists a few buttons that Command-drag won't rearrange. They are Back and Forward, Sidebar, Home, History, Downloads, and the Smart Search field. Apple's guide doesn't say whether dragging in edit mode works for them, so test it before you rely on it.
Worked example: tidy the toolbar in a few minutes

Say you want one new button and one old one gone. Start with View > Customize Toolbar. Drag the new button from the palette until the plus sign appears, then drop it where you want it. Next, hold Command and drag the old button off the bar.

If the new button sits in the wrong place, drag it along the bar. Click Done when you finish. Then look at both ends of the toolbar, and check the right edge for angle brackets. The whole pass is quick, so repeat it whenever the bar starts to feel cluttered.
Click Done and check the result

Click Done every time you finish. Apple's steps end there, and the bar returns to normal use. Check the right edge after you click Done, because that is where items hide when the window is narrow. A quick look is enough.
Fix a toolbar that is hidden or cut off

Most toolbar trouble comes from three causes. The toolbar is hidden. The window is too narrow. Or you are in full screen, where the bar can disappear. Each cause has a fix in Apple's guide, and the table below lists them.

For a hidden toolbar, choose View > Show Toolbar. In full screen, choose View > Always Show Toolbar in Full Screen to keep the toolbar visible. Apple's guide gives this option for full screen specifically, so use it there.

For a narrow window, look for angle brackets at the right end of the toolbar. They mean some items don't fit. Enlarge the window, or click the brackets to reach hidden items. Apple's general toolbar help also describes a More Items pop-up menu for the same problem in other apps.

blocks.text: Change the tab layout, which changes the toolbar

Tab layout changes how much of the toolbar you see, so it belongs in this guide. Go to Safari > Settings > Tabs and find the Tab layout setting. Separate keeps tabs in a bar below the toolbar. Compact moves tabs up into the toolbar.

With Compact, the active tab becomes the Smart Search field. Compact was missing in macOS Tahoe 26.0 to 26.3. Apple brought it back in macOS 26.4, released March 24, 2026. Apple's 26.4 notes say it gives you more space to browse. Some older articles say Compact cannot come back, but they predate that release.
Web apps have their own simplified toolbar

If you added a site to the Dock, it runs as a web app. To make one, go to the website in Safari. Click Share in the toolbar, choose Add to Dock, then click Add. Apple says the web app icon is added to the Dock and Spotlight Applications.

Apple describes a simplified toolbar for web apps. If you were signed in on the site, you are usually signed in to the web app too, and your user name and password stay the same. Apple's Safari page also mentions separate settings for web apps.

Apple's pages don't describe customizing a web app toolbar with the steps above. Treat those steps as the Safari window only. Safari has no separate web version, so web app here means a site added to the Dock.
Common mistakes with the Safari toolbar

items: Dragging without Command to remove. Plain drags add and reorder. Only Command-drag removes.
Trying Option or Shift. Apple documents only Command for this task, so don't count on other keys.
Command-dragging Back, Forward, Sidebar, Home, History, Downloads, or Smart Search to move it. Apple says that doesn't work.
Leaving edit mode open. Click Done so the bar returns to normal.
Ignoring the angle brackets. They hide items you may still want.
Expecting display options. Apple's guide doesn't confirm icon or text choices for Safari.

blocks.text: Restore a missing default button

A default button can stay gone after you remove it. Apple's help pages don't explain how to restore the default set. Apple Community threads describe a workaround: open Customize Toolbar and drag the default items back onto the bar. I could not confirm that workaround on Apple's own pages, so check the bar after each drag.
What Apple's guide leaves out of the dialog
Apple's guide covers the palette, the drag steps, and Done. It says Do any of the following and then lists those steps. It doesn't describe other options in the dialog.

Apple's Mac Help says some toolbars have a Show pop-up under Customize Toolbar. It doesn't name a Safari option in that list. Some guides mention Icon and text, Icon only, or Text only. I could not confirm those choices for Safari, so don't rely on them.
Which macOS and Safari versions these steps cover

Apple's current pages list macOS 27 first in their version selector, so these steps follow macOS 27 and Safari 27.0. Apple's Safari page says it was tested with prerelease Safari 27.0. 9to5Mac says macOS 27 shipped on Monday, September 14, 2026.

I did not check these steps on macOS Tahoe 26 or Sequoia 15. If your menus look different, confirm your macOS version before you compare. The exact Safari 27 build on your Mac may also differ from the one Apple tested.
How much Safari matters on desktop

Safari is not the most used desktop browser. StatCounter's worldwide chart for October 2026 shows Safari at 7.83%, Chrome at 66.98%, and Edge at 13.24%. That chart covers all desktop systems, not Mac alone, so it does not show a Mac-only share.
What to do next

Change one thing at a time. Add a button, click Done, and check the bar. Then move on to the next change. If the bar still looks wrong, check the window width and the tab layout before you go further.

For tabs, read [how to create a tab group in Safari on Mac](/how-to/create-a-tab-group-in-safari). For site permissions, read [how to block pop-ups in Safari on Mac](/how-to/block-pop-ups-in-safari). Both guides cover Safari settings you may need next.

faq.question: Can I customize the Safari toolbar without a keyboard shortcut?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose View > Customize Toolbar, drag the buttons you want, and click Done. Apple documents only the Command key for removing and rearranging buttons, so you don't need any other shortcut for this task.

faq.question: Why won't Command-drag move my Back button?
faq.answer: Apple lists Back and Forward among the items that Command-drag does not rearrange. Apple's guide doesn't say whether dragging inside edit mode works for them, so test that on your Mac.

faq.question: Why is Compact missing from my Safari tab settings?
faq.answer: Apple's notes say Compact was absent in macOS Tahoe 26.0 to 26.3. It returned in macOS 26.4, released March 24, 2026. Update macOS, then check Safari > Settings > Tabs again.

faq.question: Do these steps work on macOS Tahoe or Sequoia?
faq.answer: I did not verify them there. Apple's current pages show macOS 27 and Safari 27.0, so menu names may differ on older releases. Check the steps against your own menus.

faq.question: What is the difference between Show Toolbar and Customize Toolbar?
faq.answer: Show Toolbar brings back a toolbar that is hidden. Customize Toolbar changes which buttons appear and where they sit. You need the bar visible before you can customize it.

faq.question: Can I change a web app's toolbar the same way?
faq.answer: Apple's pages don't describe customizing a web app toolbar with these steps. Apple says web apps have a simplified toolbar and separate settings, so treat these steps as Safari window only.

steps.name: Open the View menu
steps.text: Open Safari and bring its window to the front. Click View in the menu bar. If the toolbar is hidden, choose Show Toolbar first, because you can't customize a bar you can't see.
steps.tip: Apple's Mac Help lists both Hide Toolbar and Show Toolbar under View, so the item you see depends on the current state.

steps.name: Choose Customize Toolbar
steps.text: Click View, then choose Customize Toolbar. The toolbar enters edit mode, and a palette of buttons appears.
steps.tip: Apple's steps for adding, moving, and removing buttons all start from this screen.

steps.name: Add a button from the palette
steps.text: Drag a button from the palette toward the bar. Keep dragging until a plus sign appears under the pointer, then release it where you want the button.
steps.tip: Wait for the plus sign before you let go. Apple's Mac Help describes it as the step to watch for.

steps.name: Rearrange buttons on the bar
steps.text: Drag a button left or right along the bar to change its place. You can also hold Command and drag a button on the toolbar to move it directly, which Apple documents as a separate method.
steps.tip: Back, Forward, Sidebar, Home, History, Downloads, and the Smart Search field do not move with Command-drag.

steps.name: Remove a button
steps.text: Hold the Command (⌘) key and drag the button off the bar. Let go when it leaves the bar. The button disappears from the toolbar.
steps.tip: Plain dragging does not remove a button. You can drag it back from the palette later.

steps.name: Click Done
steps.text: Click Done when you finish. This ends the editing session and returns the bar to normal use. Apple's steps end here for every change in this guide.
steps.tip: Make Done a habit, so the bar never stays in edit mode by accident.

steps.name: Check the buttons that won't move
steps.text: Command-drag does not rearrange Back and Forward, Sidebar, Home, History, Downloads, or the Smart Search field, according to Apple. Apple's guide doesn't say whether dragging in edit mode works for them, so test it first.
steps.tip: Test one button at a time, then click Done.

steps.name: Keep the toolbar visible in full screen
steps.text: In full screen, choose View > Always Show Toolbar in Full Screen. Apple's guide gives this option for keeping the toolbar visible in full screen.
menuPath: Always Show Toolbar in Full Screen
steps.tip: Use this option only if the toolbar keeps sliding away in full screen.

steps.name: Enlarge the window for hidden items
steps.text: Look for angle brackets at the right end of the toolbar. They mean the window is too narrow to show every item. Enlarge the window, or click the brackets to reach the items that don't fit.
steps.tip: Narrow windows hide items first, so check the right edge after every change.

steps.name: Check the tab layout
steps.text: Choose Safari > Settings > Tabs and find Tab layout. Separate keeps tabs in a bar below the toolbar. Compact moves tabs into the toolbar, and the active tab becomes the Smart Search field.
steps.tip: Compact returned in macOS 26.4, released March 24, 2026, after it was missing in 26.0 to 26.3.

shortcuts.action: Move a toolbar button directly on the bar

troubleshooting.fix: Choose View > Show Toolbar. In full screen, choose View > Always Show Toolbar in Full Screen.

troubleshooting.problem: Angle brackets sit at the right edge
troubleshooting.fix: The window is too narrow for every item. Enlarge the window or click the brackets to reach the rest.

troubleshooting.problem: Command-drag won't move Back, Forward, or Sidebar
troubleshooting.fix: Apple lists these as exceptions to Command-drag rearranging. Test dragging in edit mode, and leave them in place if that fails.
Apple's help pages don't cover this. Apple Community threads report that switching Tab layout to Separate in Safari > Settings > Tabs helped. I could not confirm that on Apple's pages.

Apple's help pages don't explain how to restore the default set. Apple Community threads describe dragging the default items back onto the bar. Check each drop, since I could not confirm this on Apple's pages.

troubleshooting.problem: The Compact tab option is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Compact was absent in macOS Tahoe 26.0 to 26.3. Update to macOS 26.4 or later, which Apple released on March 24, 2026.
